name: Polydatin
short: Only with palmitoylethanolamide: no adverse events in a trial of 70 children with IBS; no serious side effects in an open-label study of 30 women with endometriosis. No human data on polydatin alone.
text: No human safety study of polydatin on its own was found; the human data come from products combining it with palmitoylethanolamide. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial of this combination in 70 children aged 10 to 17 with irritable bowel syndrome, no adverse events were recorded. In an open-label study of 30 women with endometriosis who wished to become pregnant, who took palmitoylethanolamide alone for 10 days and then the combination for 80 days, the treatment did not show any serious side effect, although the small, open-label design limits this finding. A 2026 review of polydatin delivery systems stated that evidence on repeat-dose toxicity and immunogenicity of these formulations remains limited and that no clinical study of a polydatin nanocarrier was identified. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
